payload.title: poc.py keeps a hand-written substring rule for 'which files are migrations' in compute_fingerprint (and surface_of_path) beside the SCHEMA_REGISTRY owner it now reads in detect_sql_enums, so the report line 'TypeORM migrations' counts 340 files while the registry owns 294
evidence: tools/aria-poc/poc.py:1624 (the number is printed in the report as the TypeORM migration count)
tools/aria-poc/poc.py:250-251 (surface_of_path tags any path containing /migrations/ as migration, a second substring rule)
tools/aria-poc/poc.py:946-964 (registered_migration_patterns, the owner of the same fact)
apps/db-migrate/src/schema-registry.ts:170 (auth migrations live in src/migrations/, which the substring rule does not count)
payload.rule_violated: Single owner per concept (CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 2): one definition of which files are migrations
payload.notes: On the tracked tree at this revision the substring rule counts 340 .ts files and the registry's globs match 294. 138 counted files match no registry glob (99 of them under .archive/) and 92 files the registry does name (auth, admin-api, event-store and messaging src/migrations/) are not counted, so the fingerprint's migration_count is wrong in both directions and is printed as the migration count. The migration test in surface_of_path agrees with neither: its substring rule matches 502 tracked .ts paths, 208 of them outside every registry glob. Close condition: Derive migration_count from registered_migration_patterns and let surface_of_path use the same predicate; closed when a test over the tracked tree asserts migration_count equals the registry-matched file count and no /migrations/ substring rule remains in poc.py. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 2b). Verified at head b2259fe03f of open pull request #2151; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
